mainTopic: Which צרעת days count toward נזירות; טומאה, shaving and entering the מקדש; and quoting a chain of tradition
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about a נזיר who became a מצורע. The days of counting (ימי ספרו) and of confirmed צרעת do not count toward his נזירות, but quarantine days and the days of a זב or זבה do count. The גמרא then uses a line from that ברייתא to show that confirmed צרעת days do not count even in a long נזירות, which refutes רב חסדא. A new משנה follows. רבי אליעזר, quoting רבי יהושע, teaches that liability for entering the מקדש with טומאת מת matches whether that טומאה makes a נזיר shave, and רבי מאיר objects from the case of a שרץ. The גמרא shows from a ברייתא that רבי אליעזר actually heard the rule through a middle person, רבי יהושע בר ממל. It learns that when a teaching passes through three people, we name only the first and the last. It supports this from נחום הלבלר's chain of tradition, which skips יהושע and כלב. Finally, רבי עקיבא offers a קל וחומר that a נזיר should shave for touching a רביעית דם, and רבי יהושע answers that the rule is a received הלכה, which logic cannot extend.

steps.title: The days of counting are treated like the days of confirmed leprosy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא compares ימי ספרו to ימי חלוטו in two ways. Both need shaving, and neither counts toward the נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the days of his confirmed leprosy need shaving, so do his days of counting. And just as the days of his confirmed leprosy do not count toward his נזירות, his days of counting do not count either.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its comparison. The seven 'counting days' after the מצורע is healed get the same two rules as the days when he was fully leprous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison has two parts. Since both periods require shaving, the ברייתא links them for the second rule too: neither period counts toward the נזיר's tally of days.

keyTerms.meaning: A confirmed, fully declared מצורע
Shaving, as required for a purifying מצורע
His days of counting: the seven days a healed מצורע counts before his final purification
Count for him as part of the tally of נזירות days

phrases.english: Just as the days of his confirmed leprosy require shaving,
so too the days of his counting require shaving.
phrases.notes: These are the seven days a healed מצורע counts between his first and second shaving (ויקרא 14:8-9).

phrases.english: And just as the days of his confirmed leprosy
do not count toward his tally of נזירות days,
so too the days of his counting do not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה יְמֵי חִלּוּטוֹ טָעוּן תִּגְלַחַת אַף יְמֵי סְפָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's earlier ruling that ימי חלוטו do not count, now extending it to ימי ספרו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ימי ספרו are like ימי חלוטו. They require shaving and do not count toward the נזירות.

steps.title: Should the quarantine days also not count?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that ימי הסגרו might also be excluded. Its reason is that a quarantined מצורע, like a confirmed one, makes משכב ומושב impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the quarantine days are also like this. Logic seems to say so: a confirmed מצורע makes what he lies or sits on impure, and so does a quarantined one. So if the confirmed days do not count, the quarantine days should not count either.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible extension of the rule, using a logical comparison. This sets up the next step, which will knock the argument down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument finds one thing both stages share: both make משכב ומושב impure. From that shared feature it tries to carry over the rule that the days don't count. The question is whether this is the right shared feature to compare.

keyTerms.meaning: His days of quarantine, when he is isolated while the כהן waits to see the affliction develop
One might have thought (introduces an idea that will be rejected)
And logic dictates
Items he lies or sits on, which become impure

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה. 'יכול' signals an idea the ברייתא is about to reject.

phrases.english: One might think that even his days of quarantine are the same?
And logic supports this:
a confirmed leper makes impure what he lies on and sits on,
and during his days of quarantine he also makes impure what he lies on and sits on.
If you learned about the days of his confirmed leprosy
that they do not count toward his tally,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְמֵי הֶסְגֵּרוֹ אֵין עוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: then his days of quarantine should also not count toward his tally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule just given for ימי חלוטו and ימי ספרו should reach ימי הסגרו too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limitation of the 'does not count' rule to ימי חלוטו and ימי ספרו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since quarantine and confirmed leprosy share the impurity of משכב ומושב, they should share the rule that the days do not count.

steps.title: Rejecting the comparison: quarantine needs no shaving or offering
steps.stepSummary: The argument is rejected. Confirmed leprosy needs shaving and a קרבן, but quarantine needs neither, so the quarantine days may count.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can answer: No. The confirmed days don't count because confirmed leprosy needs shaving and an offering. The quarantine days need no shaving and no offering, so they should count toward the tally.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the comparison from step 2. It shows a stronger difference between the two stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making משכב ומושב impure is not what decides the matter. Shaving and bringing a קרבן are what link a period to the נזיר's tally. Quarantine has neither, so it is not like confirmed leprosy here.

keyTerms.meaning: You can say: No (a standard way to reject a logical argument)
Offering, which a confirmed מצורע brings when purified
Therefore

phrases.english: You can say: No,
if you said this about the days of his confirmed leprosy,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן חִלּוּטוֹ טָעוּן תִּגְלַחַת וּמֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן,
phrases.english: that is because his confirmed leprosy requires shaving and he brings an offering,
therefore those days do not count.
Will you say the same about his days of quarantine,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין טָעוּן תִּגְלַחַת, וְאֵינוֹ מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן,
phrases.english: which do not require shaving, and for which he does not bring an offering?
Therefore they should count toward the tally.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ לֹא אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִּימֵי חִלּוּטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the logical comparison proposed in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole argument that ימי הסגרו should not count.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison used the wrong shared feature. Confirmed leprosy has shaving and a קרבן, which quarantine lacks, and those are what matter here.

steps.title: Final rule: which days count and which do not
steps.stepSummary: Summary ruling: ימי ספרו and ימי גמרו do not count toward the נזירות. The days of a זב, a זבה, and a מצורע's quarantine do count.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: the days of counting and the days of confirmed leprosy do not count toward his tally. But the days of a זב, a זבה, and the quarantine of a מצורע do count for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sums up the whole discussion in one clear rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ימי ספרו and ימי גמרו (another name for ימי חלוטו) are excluded. ימי הסגרו now count, following step 3. The ברייתא also adds זב and זבה to the list of impurities whose days still count.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said (introduces a rule drawn from what came before)
His days of 'completion', meaning the days of confirmed leprosy
A man or woman made impure by a bodily discharge

steps.whatToRemember: For a נזיר: ימי ספרו and ימי חלוטו (גמרו) of צרעת do not count toward his נזירות. Quarantine days, and the days of זב and זבה, do count.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברייתא does not decide whether impure days count by the shared impurity of משכב ומושב. What sets confirmed צרעת apart from quarantine is the shaving and קרבן it requires.

phrases.english: From here they said:
the days of his counting and the days of his full leprosy
phrases.notes: Literally 'his completion.' It means the same as חלוט, the fully confirmed מצורע.

phrases.english: do not count toward his tally.
But the days of a man with a discharge and a woman with a discharge
and the quarantine of a leper
these do count for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ יְמֵי סְפָרוֹ וִימֵי גְמָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of steps 1 and 3 as a practical rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ימי ספרו and ימי גמרו do not count toward the נזירות. The days of זב, זבה, and הסגר of a מצורע do count.

steps.title: Pulling a proof line from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes its line that the days of טומאה are different from the days of confirmed צרעת, because only the days of טומאה cancel the earlier days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyway, the ברייתא teaches: No! You can say this about days of טומאה, because they cancel the earlier days. Can you say the same about his days of confirmed צרעת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It quotes one specific line from the ברייתא that it will now examine closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line says that days of confirmed צרעת do not cancel the days the נזיר already kept, unlike days of טומאת מת. The גמרא wants to use this line against רב חסדא, who said these days do count in a long נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. The גמרא uses this phrase to pull out the one line it needs for a proof.
The days a נזיר is impure from a dead body
Cancels the earlier days, so the נזיר has to start counting again
The days of his confirmed צרעת

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
No, if you say this about days of impurity,
since they cancel the earlier days,
would you say it about his days of confirmed leprosy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from Steps 1-4 and takes one line from it to use as a proof.
steps.raayaObject: Whether days of confirmed צרעת count toward a long נזירות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line that sets days of טומאה apart from days of confirmed צרעת
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that the days of confirmed צרעת count toward a long נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the days of חלוטו do not count. Steps 6-7 show this must refer to a long נזירות, which contradicts רב חסדא.

steps.title: Which kind of נזירות is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. It rules out a short נזירות, because there the days could not count anyway, since hair must grow for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is this? If you say it is a short נזירות, that can't be, because we need hair growth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of נזירות the ברייתא has in mind. It rejects the first option, a short נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A short נזירות is thirty days. A נזיר needs a full thirty days of hair growth after he becomes pure, so in a short נזירות the צרעת days could never count no matter what. The ברייתא would have no reason to teach this, so it must be talking about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case? What situation is being talked about?
A short נזירות of thirty days
Hair growth. A נזיר needs a stretch of time when his hair grows.

phrases.english: In what case?
If you say it is a short naziriteship,
but we require hair growth!
phrases.notes: He needs thirty days of growth after becoming pure. In a short נזירות, that leaves no room for the צרעת days to count anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the line quoted in Step 5 is talking about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ברייתא talking about a short נזירות or a long one?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not a short one, because then the days could not count anyway, since hair growth is required.

steps.title: Even in a long נזירות, the צרעת days do not count
steps.stepSummary: So the ברייתא must mean a long נזירות, and it still says the days do not count. This proves that days of confirmed צרעת never count, and the גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about a long נזירות? And still it teaches that the days do not count toward his total. So we see they do not count for him! Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The ברייתא must be talking about a long נזירות, and even there the days of confirmed צרעת are not counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a long נזירות there would be enough time left for hair growth, so the צרעת days could have counted. The ברייתא still says they do not, which goes against רב חסדא's view that they count in a long נזירות. The words שמע מינה show the גמרא accepts this.

keyTerms.meaning: A long נזירות, longer than thirty days
Count toward his total number of days
So we see. It introduces the conclusion that follows.
Learn from it. The proof stands.

steps.whatToRemember: Days of confirmed צרעת do not count toward נזירות, even in a long נזירות where there would be time for hair growth.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final ruling against the view that צרעת days count in a long נזירות.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about a lengthy naziriteship,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי שֶׁאֵין עוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: and it teaches that they do not count toward his tally.
Apparently, they do not count for him!
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Short נזירות was ruled out in Step 6, so this step reads the line as a long נזירות and draws the conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Days of confirmed צרעת never count toward נזירות. This goes against רב חסדא, who said they count in a long נזירות.

steps.title: משנה: Shaving for a טומאה and liability for entering the מקדש go together
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר quotes רבי יהושע. Any טומאת מת that makes a נזיר shave also makes a person liable for entering the מקדש. Any טומאת מת that does not make a נזיר shave does not make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר said in the name of רבי יהושע: For any טומאה from a dead body that a נזיר must shave for, one is liable for entering the מקדש. And for any טומאה from a dead body that a נזיר does not shave for, one is not liable for entering the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It ties two laws together: when a נזיר must shave for a טומאה, and when a person is liable for entering the מקדש while impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע uses the נזיר's shaving as a measuring stick. If a type of טומאת מת is strong enough to make a נזיר shave, entering the מקדש with it brings liability. If it is not, entering the מקדש with it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה. The marker מַתְנִי׳ shows a new משנה is starting.
Impurity that comes from a dead body
Shaves. A נזיר who becomes impure shaves his hair.
Entering the מקדש. A person who is impure may not enter it.
Liable to be punished, or to bring a קרבן

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
Any impurity from a corpse
for which a nazirite shaves,
one is liable for it for entering the Temple.
And any impurity from a corpse
for which the nazirite does not shave,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: one is not liable for it for entering the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, separate from the צרעת discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for entering the מקדש with טומאת מת exactly matches whether that טומאה makes a נזיר shave.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: It can't be weaker than a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר objects. A טומאת מת that a נזיר does not shave for should not be more lenient than the טומאה of a שרץ, and a שרץ does make one liable for entering the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: This should not be more lenient than a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר argues against the second half of רבי יהושע's rule, the part that says there is no liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who becomes impure from a שרץ is liable if he enters the מקדש. טומאת מת is more serious than שרץ, so even the kinds a נזיר does not shave for must also bring liability. In רבי מאיר's view, the shaving rule cannot be used to measure liability for the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A small creeping animal whose dead body makes a person impure
More lenient, a lighter level of impurity

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not talking about the נזיר's shaving. He only disagrees about liability for entering the מקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תְּהֵא זוֹ קַלָּה מִן הַשֶּׁרֶץ.
phrases.english: This should not be more lenient than a creeping animal.
phrases.notes: "This" is a טומאת מת that a נזיר does not shave for. Someone impure from a שרץ is already liable for entering the מקדש (ויקרא 5:2-3).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: לֹא תְּהֵא זוֹ קַלָּה מִן הַשֶּׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רבי יהושע's rule in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that a טומאת מת a נזיר does not shave for brings no liability for entering the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר argument: טומאת שרץ is a lighter impurity and still brings liability, so any טומאת מת, which is stronger, must bring liability too.

steps.title: Did רבי אליעזר really hear this from רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's attribution, because רבי אליעזר actually learned the rule through רבי יהושע בר ממל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Did רבי אליעזר really learn this in the name of רבי יהושע? But he learned it in the name of רבי יהושע בר ממל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by questioning who רבי אליעזר heard the rule from. It says he heard it from רבי יהושע בר ממל, not straight from רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 8) presented the rule as רבי אליעזר quoting רבי יהושע. The גמרא says there was a middle person, רבי יהושע בר ממל, so the chain in the משנה looks incomplete. This is a challenge about who said what, not about the rule itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned it (received it as a tradition)
But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
A חכם who passed on רבי יהושע's teaching to רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ גְּמַר לַהּ?
phrases.english: And did Rabbi Eliezer learn it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua?
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה's statement in step 8.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר מֶמֶל גְּמַר לָהּ.
phrases.english: But he learned it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua bar Memel!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ גְּמַר לַהּ? וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges who the משנה's rule (steps 8-9) is attributed to
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording: רבי אליעזר quoting רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There was a middle person in the chain, so the משנה seems to leave out רבי יהושע בר ממל

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי אליעזר meets רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי אליעזר found someone discussing this rule before רבי מאיר, who objected from the case of a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי אליעזר said: When I went to Ardaskeya, I found רבי יהושע בן פתר ראש sitting and discussing a הלכה before רבי מאיר: Any טומאת מת that a נזיר shaves for makes a person liable for entering the מקדש, and any טומאת מת that a נזיר does not shave for does not make him liable. רבי מאיר said to him: This should not be more lenient than a שרץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the challenge comes from. This first part sets the scene: the rule is stated, and רבי מאיר objects to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same rule and the same objection from steps 8-9, now told as a story. The ברייתא is setting up the key moment in the next step, where רבי אליעזר names his source.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
Ardaskeya, the name of a place
Sitting and discussing (a הלכה)
Entering the מקדש (while טמא)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer said:
When I went to Ardaskeya,

phrases.aramaic: מָצָאתִי אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פֵּתֶר רֹאשׁ
phrases.english: I found Rabbi Yehoshua ben Petter Rosh

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב וְדָן לִפְנֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר בַּהֲלָכָה:
phrases.english: who was sitting and discussing a halacha before Rabbi Meir:
Any impurity from a corpse
for which a nazir shaves
one is liable for it because of entering the Temple.
And any impurity from a corpse
for which a nazir does not shave

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: one is not liable for it because of entering the Temple.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַל תְּהֵא זוֹ קַלָּה מִשֶּׁרֶץ.
phrases.english: He said to him: This should not be more lenient than a creeping animal!
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי מאיר. This is the same objection we saw in step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: כְּשֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לְעַרְדַּסְקִיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the challenge in step 10
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that רבי אליעזר had a middle source
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא telling of רבי אליעזר's meeting with רבי מאיר

steps.title: רבי אליעזר names רבי יהושע בר ממל as his source
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר tells רבי מאיר that he heard the rule from רבי יהושע בר ממל, who quoted רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: Do you know רבי יהושע בר ממל? He said: Yes. This is what רבי יהושע בר ממל told me in the name of רבי יהושע: Any טומאת מת that a נזיר shaves for makes a person liable for entering the מקדש, and any טומאת מת that a נזיר does not shave for does not make him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends the rule by saying who he heard it from. He heard it from רבי יהושע בר ממל, who heard it from רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the key line for the גמרא's challenge. The chain clearly has three people: רבי יהושע, then רבי יהושע בר ממל, then רבי אליעזר. In the משנה only the first and last names appear.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you at all familiar with...?
Yes

phrases.english: I said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר is still speaking, now to רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם אַתָּה בָּקִי בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר מֶמֶל?
phrases.english: Are you at all familiar with Rabbi Yehoshua bar Memel?
He said to me: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָמַר לִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר מֶמֶל
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yehoshua bar Memel told me
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל טוּמְאָה מִן הַמֵּת שֶׁהַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ עָלֶיהָ
phrases.english: Any impurity from a corpse for which a nazir shaves
one is liable for it because of entering the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל טוּמְאָה מִן הַמֵּת שֶׁאֵין הַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ עָלֶיהָ
phrases.english: and any impurity from a corpse for which a nazir does not shave

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: one is not liable for it because of entering the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: כְּלוּם אַתָּה בָּקִי בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and gives the line that names the middle person in the chain
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר heard the rule through רבי יהושע בר ממל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's own words in the ברייתא

steps.title: So he learned it through רבי יהושע בר ממל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the ברייתא: רבי אליעזר learned the rule in the name of רבי יהושע בר ממל.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he learned it in the name of רבי יהושע בר ממל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the proof from the ברייתא. This makes the challenge from step 10 stronger, and the גמרא now needs to explain the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proves there was a middle person. The open question is why the משנה left him out. The next step answers that.

keyTerms.meaning: So it is (sums up a proof)
He learned it

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר מֶמֶל גְּמִיר לַהּ!
phrases.english: So he learned it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua bar Memel!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֱוֵי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר מֶמֶל גְּמִיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the ברייתא and confirms the challenge
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר received the rule through a middle person, רבי יהושע בר ממל

steps.title: With three names, we say the first and the last
steps.stepSummary: The answer: when a teaching passes through three people, we mention the first and last and leave out the middle one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Learn from this: any teaching said through three people, we mention the first and the last, but we do not mention the middle one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a general rule about quoting chains. That rule explains why the משנה names רבי יהושע and רבי אליעזר but leaves out רבי יהושע בר ממל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording was not a mistake. It follows a normal way of quoting, where the middle link is dropped. So both the משנה and the ברייתא are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this
A teaching or ruling
Through three people
The first ones and the last ones
The middle ones

steps.whatToRemember: When a teaching passes through three people, we may quote only the first and the last. That is why the משנה can say "רבי אליעזר in the name of רבי יהושע" even though רבי יהושע בר ממל was in between.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains other places in ש״ס where a statement seems to skip a link in the chain of who said it.

phrases.english: They said: Learn from this:
Any teaching that was said through three people,
the first and the last, we say,
the middle one, we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כֹּל שְׁמַעְתְּתָא דְּמִתְאַמְרָה בְּבֵי תְּלָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge confirmed in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle of quoting that explains the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's attribution seemed to leave out a needed link
steps.terutzMaskana: Dropping the middle name of three is normal practice, so the משנה is accurate

steps.title: Support from נחום הלבלר's chain of tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק supports the rule from a משנה where נחום הלבלר gives a chain of tradition back to the נביאים, about פאה for dill and mustard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this: נחום הלבלר said: This is what I received from רבי מיאשא, who received from אבא, who received from the זוגות, who received from the נביאים: It is a הלכה למשה מסיני that one who sows dill and mustard in two or three places must leave פאה from each one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a משנה as support for the rule that a chain of names can be shortened. The משנה lists a chain of teachers going back to the נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain starts with משה (a הלכה למשה מסיני) and then goes straight to the נביאים. The proof comes from the link that is missing between them, which the next step points out. The actual הלכה about פאה is just the content of the quote.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this (in a משנה)
Scribe
The "pairs" of leading חכמים in the time of the second בית המקדש
A law given orally to משה at סיני
The corner of a field left for the poor

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We, too, have learned this:
Nachum the scribe said:
This is what I received from Rabbi Meyasha,
who received it from Abba,
phrases.notes: Literally "from father"; it may mean his father or a person called אבא.

phrases.english: who received it from the pairs,
who received it from the prophets:
It is a law given to Moshe at Sinai
about one who sows dill and mustard
in two or three places,
that he leaves a corner for the poor from each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a משנה for the rule in step 14
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a chain of names can be shortened when quoted

steps.title: יהושע and כלב are left out, so the proof stands
steps.stepSummary: נחום הלבלר skipped יהושע and כלב in his chain, which proves that middle links in a tradition can be left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet he does not list יהושע and כלב. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the key detail in נחום הלבלר's chain and closes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition went from משה to the זקנים, such as יהושע and כלב, and then to the נביאים. נחום הלבלר jumps straight from משה to the נביאים. That shows it is normal to name the first and last links and skip the middle, just as the משנה in Step 8 left out רבי יהושע בר ממל.

keyTerms.meaning: He counts, lists, or mentions
Learn from this; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: When a teaching passes through three people, we may quote the first and the last and leave out the middle one. נחום הלבלר's skipping of יהושע and כלב proves it.

phrases.english: And yet Joshua and Caleb
he does not list.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָלֵב לָא קָחָשֵׁיב. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that middle links in a chain of tradition may be left out
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחום הלבלר's chain in the משנה of פאה, which leaves out יהושע and כלב
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Quoting the first and last people in a chain while skipping the middle one is legitimate.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's argument that blood should be like a small bone
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא argues by קל וחומר that a נזיר should shave for touching or carrying a רביעית דם, since he shaves for a bone the size of a barley grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי עקיבא said: I argued before רבי אליעזר. A bone the size of a barley grain does not make a person impure in a tent, yet a נזיר shaves for touching it or carrying it. A רביעית דם does make a person impure in a tent. Isn't it logical that a נזיר should shave for touching it or carrying it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי עקיבא tells about a קל וחומר he once presented to his teacher רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small bone is the weaker kind of טומאה because it does not make impure through אהל, being under the same roof. Even so, touching or carrying it makes a נזיר shave. The רביעית דם is stronger, because it does make impure through אהל, so רבי עקיבא reasons it should surely make him shave for touching or carrying too.

keyTerms.meaning: A bone of a dead person the size of a barley grain
A quarter of a לוג of blood from a dead person
Makes impure by being under the same roof
Touching and carrying
Shaves; the נזיר's shaving after becoming impure, which restarts his נזירות

phrases.english: MISHNA
Rabbi Akiva said:
I argued before Rabbi Eliezer:
If a bone the size of a barley grain,
which does not make a person impure in a tent,

phrases.aramaic: הַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ עַל מַגָּעוֹ וְעַל מַשָּׂאוֹ,
phrases.english: the nazir shaves for touching it and for carrying it,
then a quarter-log of blood,
which does make a person impure in a tent,
is it not logical that the nazir should
shave for touching it and for carrying it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דַּנְתִּי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא proposes a קל וחומר: if a נזיר shaves for touching or carrying the weaker bone, he should also shave for touching or carrying the stronger רביעית דם.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר refuses the logical argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects the קל וחומר and says we may not use one here, without giving a reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: What is this, עקיבא?! We do not argue here from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר sharply pushes back on רבי עקיבא's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not find a flaw in the logic itself. He simply says a קל וחומר is not allowed in this case. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
We do not reason or derive

phrases.english: He said to me: What is this, Akiva?!
We do not argue here from a kal vachomer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר proposed in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of a קל וחומר in this particular case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No flaw is stated yet. רבי אליעזר only says this case is not open to a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יהושע explains that it is a received rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע praises רבי עקיבא's logic but says the rule is a הלכה, so a קל וחומר cannot extend it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came and presented the matter before רבי יהושע, he said to me: You spoke well, but this is what they said: it is a הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא brings his argument to רבי יהושע, who explains why רבי אליעזר rejected it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע agrees the logic is good. But the list of things a נזיר shaves for is a fixed tradition, a הלכה, and not something built from reasoning. Since it was not built from logic, logic cannot add new cases to it.

keyTerms.meaning: I presented, laid out the argument
You spoke well; the reasoning is sound
A received rule, here a הלכה למשה מסיני

steps.whatToRemember: A rule received as a הלכה is not open to a קל וחומר. Even perfect logic cannot stretch it to new cases.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not saying the קל וחומר is badly built. He says it is good logic that simply cannot be applied to a received הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains רבי אליעזר's short refusal and shows a basic principle: rules handed down by tradition work differently from rules built by reasoning.

phrases.english: And when I came and presented the matter
before Rabbi Yehoshua,
he said to me: You spoke well,
but this is what they said: it is a halacha.
phrases.notes: He means a הלכה למשה מסיני, a rule handed down from משה. Since it comes from tradition and not from logic, a קל וחומר can't add to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָפֶה אָמַרְתָּ, אֶלָּא כֵּן אָמְרוּ: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי אליעזר's rejection in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The cases that make a נזיר shave come from a received הלכה, so a קל וחומר cannot add the רביעית דם to touching and carrying.
